turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes, so let's start with the part where my son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of class, before anyone called me.
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. I'm writing that down, 4.2, your words. Now who decided on the zero, and on what basis?
Here's the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen, read it yourself.
Did anyone sit down with Owen and hear him out before that zero went in, Hale?
If he drafted somewhere else, he can bring me that file with its dates, and I'll look at it with you.
You skipped my question. Procedure 4.1 says you speak to the student first, and so far you haven't told me you did.
Second: the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in the play. Here's the act. Search it.
Editions differ, Hale, so which edition is that, and is it the one his class was assigned? Read me the line exactly as it appears in Owen's essay.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no errors.
Forty minutes under a clock against an essay he could revise at home is not a fair comparison, Hale. And you still owe me the edition, and the line exactly as he wrote it.

Under 4.4 this is a first concern. I'm offering a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, and I want it in writing tonight with the words nothing goes on his record. Before I agree to any rewrite, Hale, you still owe me the edition and the line exactly as Owen wrote it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you acknowledged that the zero was entered before I was contacted, in breach of procedure 4.2, and you agreed to put in writing a private, supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed on Owen's record. Before I agree to that rewrite, I still require the edition of Hamlet you checked, confirmation that it is the one his class was assigned, and the line exactly as it appears in Owen's essay. I expect your written offer tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her fallback position, accepting that your 4.4 offer meets her demand that nothing goes on his record, but she still wants the edition and the exact line before agreeing to the rewrite; your offer is the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and you got there before her time ran out.
What moved her: Showing the version history with its exact times, because it was dated, on Owen's own document, and she had no answer for it except to retreat to procedure.
What cost ground: Leaving her questions unanswered, whether anyone heard Owen before the zero and which edition you checked, because each open item gave her something to hold instead of moving.
What she never said: One night in October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the writing late on the night before it was due, very close to that kind of night, which is why she went short and hard on procedure there, but it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she raised the edition defence against the Act 3, Scene 2 quotation, name the edition the class was assigned and read the line from Owen's essay right then, so that piece of evidence stands and she can move to her last position.
